notes: 25 km protective dam; 70-100m wide; 5.7m high; connected to Prypiat River via inlet/outlet structures
source: Bugai 1997 Wat Resour Res doi:10.1029/96WR03963; IAEA TECDOC-1886

context: 0.15 km³; designed for 1000 MWe of reactor cooling; maintained 7m above Pripyat River level by pumping
notes: Dam perimeter: 25 km; max depth: 18-20 m; mean depth: 6.6 m; length: ~11 km; width: ~2 km

context: Southern deeper section; north shallower (~4m mean)
notes: Stratification forms thermocline in summer; affects radionuclide vertical distribution in water column
source: IAEA TECDOC-1886; cooling pond characterization studies

context: Total activity in cooling pond water immediately post-accident from all isotopes; dominated by short-lived fission products plus Cs-137 Cs-134 Sr-90
notes: Equivalent to 370 MBq/m³; decreased rapidly as short-lived isotopes decayed and Cs-137 absorbed onto sediments

context: Cs-137 in northern part of cooling pond 1986; = 1.5 × 10⁶ Bq/m³

context: Cs-137 in southern part of cooling pond 1986 = 1.0 × 10⁶ Bq/m³
notes: Rapid sedimentation of Cs-137 onto bottom sediments within months of accident; 95% of Cs-137 absorbed by sediments

context: Cs-137 in water column after rapid sedimentation onto bottom sediments; = 2.0 × 10⁴ Bq/m³; much lower than 1986 values
notes: Cs-137 strongly sorbs onto fine-grained sediments and does NOT readily remobilize; contrast with Sr-90 which remains soluble

context: Sr-90 concentration stabilized at 1-2 kBq/m³ in cooling pond water 2000-2010; = 1 Bq/L
notes: Sr-90 much more soluble than Cs-137; only ~20% of Sr-90 absorbed by sediments vs 95% Cs-137; remainder stays mobile in water
source: Bugai 2022 Sci Rep; MDPI Water 2024 doi:10.3390/w15081504

context: Sr-90 in groundwater around cooling pond before 2014 drawdown; wide range = 0.1 to 100 Bq/L depending on proximity to contamination sources
notes: WHO drinking water guideline for Sr-90: 10000 Bq/m³ (10 Bq/L); some wells exceeded this even pre-drawdown
source: Bugai 2022 Sci Rep; Science Total Environ 2023 PMID:36739017

context: Cooling pond pumps stopped May 2014 as part of decommissioning; uncontrolled drawdown followed; water level dropped by up to 6m near dam
notes: Prior to this pond maintained artificially 7m above Pripyat River level; drawdown was planned decommissioning step
source: IAEA TECDOC-1886; Science Total Environ 2023 PMID:36739017

context: Groundwater levels decreased >50 cm at 65% of shallow monitoring wells following drawdown
notes: Up to 6m decrease in wells adjacent to cooling pond; changing hydraulic gradient altered groundwater flow directions

context: Sr-90 in Pripyat River floodplain groundwater north of ChNPP after 2014 drawdown; = 102 Bq/L
notes: Exceeds WHO drinking water guideline (10 kBq/m³ = 10 Bq/L) by ~10x; drawdown altered hydraulic gradient → increased Sr-90 flux to floodplain

context: Pre-drawdown Sr-90 in Pripyat floodplain groundwater near WHO guideline; drawdown increased by 10x
notes: Confirms drawdown caused significant increase in Sr-90 transport to floodplain; ongoing monitoring required; natural attenuation slow for Sr-90

context: Cs-137 total inventory in cooling pond bottom sediments; 2012 measurement; ± 2.59 TBq; = 16.28 TBq
notes: 95% of initial Cs-137 input now in sediments; sediment-bound Cs-137 not readily remobilized; controls long-term water concentration
source: Distribution and Dynamics Springer 2020 chapter; IAEA TECDOC-1886

context: Sr-90 total inventory in cooling pond bottom sediments; ± 0.48 TBq; = 2.4 TBq; 80% associated with fuel particles
notes: Lower sorption fraction than Cs-137; ~80% of sediment Sr-90 in fuel particle matrix (slowly dissolving); fuel particle dissolution = slow-release Sr-90 source for decades

context: Pu-239+240 in cooling pond sediments; = 5.18 GBq; ± 1.48 GBq; >80% in fuel particles

source: Distribution and Dynamics Springer 2020; IAEA TECDOC-1886

context: ~20% of total Sr-90 in water/porewater + exchangeable fraction vs ~80% in non-exchangeable (fuel particle) form

source: IAEA TECDOC-1886; Distribution and Dynamics Springer 2020

context: Peak Cs-137 in fish in cooling pond immediately post-accident; all species affected; levels not representative of sustained values

context: Cs-137 in pike and perch 1987; 1-2 kBq/kg wet weight; EU limit is 1250 Bq/kg for fish

context: Perch Cs-137 in Kiev Reservoir (Dnieper km 890; 300 km downstream from Chernobyl); 2001

context: ISF-2 Interim Dry Spent Nuclear Fuel Storage Facility obtained operating license April 26 2021 (exact 35th anniversary)
notes: First transportation of spent fuel in operating mode: June 8 2021; co-located adjacent to cooling pond; HOLTEC design; 100-year design life

context: 1698 fuel assemblies stored in ISF-2 as of January 2022; transfer from ISF-1 wet storage ongoing
notes: Design capacity 21217 assemblies; all 4 reactor units' spent fuel to be transferred from wet storage ISF-1 to dry cask ISF-2; ISF-1 (wet) to be decommissioned

context: Largest dry spent nuclear fuel storage facility in world (by capacity for single accident/site); HOLTEC HISTORE modular cask system
notes: Each dry cask contains separated fuel assemblies from Chernobyl Units 1-3 (Unit 4 core destroyed); 100-year interim storage until permanent repository

context: ISF-2 dry casks provide multi-barrier containment: fuel matrix + cladding + canister + dry cask + storage building; normal dose rates outside building are background levels
notes: Comparison: ISF-1 (wet storage) required continuous water cooling and monitoring for 35 years; ISF-2 passively safe with no electrical cooling requirement

context: 28+ years continuous Cs-137 monitoring in Kyiv dam reservoir (serving Kiev water supply for ~9 million people)
